reason: E1 supports that high configurational entropy stabilizes simple solid solutions at high temperatures, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that lattice distortion reduces atomic diffusivity or that sluggish diffusion suppresses phase segregation. E2 mentions distortion effects for electronic properties and catalytic performance, not for diffusion or thermal stability. The core mechanistic premise linking distortion to sluggish diffusion and high-temperature stability is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid solution phase at high temperatures.
Lattice distortion (from atomic size mismatch) reduces atomic diffusivity.
Reduced diffusivity (sluggish diffusion) suppresses phase segregation and chemical ordering.
The synergy of entropy stabilization and sluggish diffusion maintains structural/chemical homogeneity up to 1923 K.
Greater lattice distortion leads to better stability than lower distortion at similar mixing entropy.
